text:
The adverse possession period most likely began when the tenant's possession became hostile, not in 1986 when he stopped paying rent. Stopping rent alone does not repudiate the owner's title, and a tenant's occupancy is presumed permissive, so the clock more plausibly started when the lease expired in 1992 and he held over while openly claiming ownership (or after an earlier clear, communicated repudiation). That reading puts the 20-year period's end around 2012, after the Boy Scouts' 2009 discovery, but the exact date depends on this jurisdiction's holdover and repudiation rules. This corrects my earlier answer, and the team note is also wrong: the origin of a tenant's possession does matter.
